title: The anti-obesity effects of a tuna peptide on 3T3-L1 adipocytes are mediated by the inhibition of the expression of lipogenic and adipogenic genes and by the activation of the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway

citation.title: The anti-obesity effects of a tuna peptide on 3T3-L1 adipocytes are mediated by the inhibition of the expression of lipogenic and adipogenic genes and by the activation of the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway

what_it_measured.text: The anti-obesity effects of a tuna peptide on 3T3-L1 adipocytes are mediated by the inhibition of the expression of lipogenic and adipogenic genes and by the activation of the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway

dose.text: Following differentiation, 3T3‑L1 cells were treated with the tuna‑derived peptide, D‑I‑V‑D‑K‑I‑E‑I (TP‑D) (500 or 1,000 ng/ml), for 48 h.

endpoint.text: The inhibition of lipid accumulation was measured using a glucose and triglyceride (TG) assay.
The test enzyme (TG‑measured solution) was added to the lysate supernatants, and the cells were maintained at 37˚C for 5 min in a humidified atmosphere containing 5% CO2.
Cell viability was measured at 490 nm using by MTS assay.

reported_results.text: The most significant decrease in the TG levels was observed at the dose of 500 and 1,000 ng/ml.
The TG levels in the 3T3‑L1 cells decreased significantly and in a dose‑dependent manner following treatment with TP‑D at 125, 250, 500 and 1,000 ng/ml for 48 h.
